bug_semantics: The unauthenticated /reset_password handler generated an absolute password-reset URL with Flask url_for(..., _external=True). Because the application did not configure SERVER_NAME, Flask derived that URL's authority from the request Host header. An attacker could submit a reset request for a victim with an attacker-controlled Host; the emailed link then sent the reset token to the attacker's host when the victim followed it, enabling the attacker to use the token and take over the account.
flaw_origin: fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d is the smallest causal introducer: it changed the existing reset-request stub in hashview/users/routes.py into a working token-email flow and first added url_for('users.reset_token', token=token, _external=True), while that commit's tree had no SERVER_NAME configuration. The direct parent had only a pass-through send_reset_email stub and contained neither the external reset-link call nor any _external=True occurrence. Later edits guarded unknown users, added user_id, and reformatted the message but preserved the same Host-derived authority mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object (git cat-file -p fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d) names author and committer i128 <jarsnah12@gmail.com>, has the message 'restructuring', and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/hashview/hashview/issues/145 identifies CVE-2025-43930, states v0.8.1 and earlier are affected, links https://github.com/hashview/hashview/blob/579a082176279f4af0e128e44c9da5667f82ec5a/hashview/users/routes.py#L198-L218, and describes the malicious-Host password-reset-poisoning path; the maintainer's 2026-06-01 comment says it is fixed in the latest release. At 579a082176279f4af0e128e44c9da5667f82ec5a, hashview/users/routes.py:176-195 contains the public reset flow and _external=True reset URL (the same file also contains the admin reset variant at lines 198-218). git log -L 176,196:hashview/users/routes.py at that revision traces the external public reset URL through formatting and parameter changes back to fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d; an all-Python git log -S'_external=True' likewise returns fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d as the earliest occurrence. The BIC diff shows it replacing the parent's pass-only send_reset_email path with token creation, an emailed external URL, and send_email. Direct-parent command git grep -n -e '_external=True' -e "url_for('users.reset_token'" a64d8ea9dd6363ff4dc4303024b3b93a0a9b9c5c -- hashview/users/routes.py returned no matches; git grep SERVER_NAME on the BIC tree also returned no matches. For the affected boundary, 998eb824e5487ec21a32fa952cd8987194c1732e records the v0.8.1-Beta 2023-08-18 release in CHANGELOG.md; its tree declares __version__ = '0.8.1', retains _external=True in hashview/users/routes.py, has no SERVER_NAME in hashview/config.py, setup.py, or hashview/config.conf.example, and has fb34913357030c170c6e7d6ab64989c6c684fa5d as its merge base. Direct fix https://github.com/hashview/hashview/commit/447295469db2d2bbfb0bab62fa5af4581d3509f8 corrects setup.py's broken config.write expression so first-run setup writes SERVER_NAME = <fqdn>:<port>; hashview/config.py reads that value and hashview/__init__.py loads Config into Flask. First-party PR https://github.com/hashview/hashview/pull/163 says it merges v0.8.2 to main; merge 8d377f2886389150d5d3ece8c177285c6731eefc has parents e5142a4c8357e8f12aaa51d799104c4ff9787406 and 99f178ab33adc4eca93a2e24365f85b0538eec3a, with only the second-parent side containing direct fix 447295469db2d2bbfb0bab62fa5af4581d3509f8. Release commit 99f178ab33adc4eca93a2e24365f85b0538eec3a declares __version__ = '0.8.2', dates v0.8.2-Beta to 2026-06-01, contains the direct fix, and its setup.py/config.py/config.conf.example consistently write/read/document SERVER_NAME. CHANGELOG.md explicitly lists the fixed setup.py parenthesis bug and the new stored server FQDN/port. The clone has no refs/tags (git for-each-ref refs/tags returned empty), so the first-party in-tree version and dated release commits are the available boundary evidence rather than tag membership. fix_sha corrected from 8d377f2886389150d5d3ece8c177285c6731eefc to 168d8e3f4f686161d61f9fa15f677c23f5ce55e3 (direct); merged by 8d377f2886389150d5d3ece8c177285c6731eefc (reconciliation 2026-08-29: R names 168d8e3f4f686161d61f9fa15f677c23f5ce55e3 ('Massive internal changes', i128, 2025-11-10): `git show 168d8e3f -- hashview/users/routes.py` changes `{url_for('users.reset_token', user_id=user.id, token=token, _external=True)}` -> `_external=False` AND first adds SERVER_NAME ) fix_sha normalized to bare 40-hex 168d8e3f4f686161d61f9fa15f677c23f5ce55e3 (gate format; basis unchanged, reconciliation 2026-08-29).
reasoning: Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). The vulnerable capability did not exist in the direct parent: the public route called a send_reset_email function whose body was pass, and there was no external reset URL. The BIC made the flow operational and chose _external=True without establishing a trusted canonical authority, so it is causal rather than a later move or formatting change. git log -L and repository-wide -S history both identify that same commit as the first writer, and direct-parent tree inspection proves absence. The BIC predates and is present in the affected v0.8.1 release tree. An attempted v0.8.2 SERVER_NAME setup path was ineffective because setup.py parenthesized config.write before concatenating the value; direct fix 447295469db2d2bbfb0bab62fa5af4581d3509f8 made the installer persist the canonical host, which Config loads into Flask, and that commit reached main through release merge 8d377f2886389150d5d3ece8c177285c6731eefc before/in the dated v0.8.2 release tree. Finally, the exact BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer identity and no AI attribution marker, so the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
